rounds.text: Rashi Peripherals Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 16.8x that sits well below the sector benchmark of 20.77x [E1, E6]. This modest valuation clashes sharply with stellar operational momentum, highlighted by a 40% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 50% compounded profit growth over the same period [E16, E19]. Fundamental quality is equally robust, with a return on capital employed of 17.0% easily outstripping the sector median ROCE of 12.1% [E12, E67]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation metrics show immense untapped upside, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 1725 per share—granting a massive 53.2% margin of safety over the current market price of Rs 807 [E40, E41]. The market's low expectations are further exposed by a reverse DCF, which reveals that today's price prices in a meager 5.6% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 16.0% [E42]. Conceded: cash conversion stands at just 0.40x of reported profit for March 2026, meaning profits are running far ahead of operating cash flow [E28]. This high-conviction setup scores an impressive 93 out of 100 on rules-based screens, driven by powerful year-over-year sales and net profit surges [E56, E57, E59].

A severe disconnect between headline earnings and actual cash generation undermines the reported financial health of the business [E28]. Operating cash flow stands at a meager 0.40x of reported profit for March 2026, meaning profits are racing far ahead of actual cash collection and signaling potential risks in receivables or accruals [E28]. This weak cash conversion leaves operating cash flow at only 41% of operating profit, exposing a heavy reliance on non-cash accounting items [E31]. Furthermore, total borrowings have expanded to Rs 991 Cr in March 2026, up from Rs 910 Cr in the previous year, compounding the strain from inadequate cash collection [E34]. Institutional sentiment is also cooling, evidenced by domestic institutions trimming their stake to 12.68% from 14.41% and an overall negative institutional money flow of -2.28 percentage points [E38, E39]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing twelve-month sales growth of 40% and a high relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E16, E46].

While the bear highlights a low cash conversion of 0.40x for March 2026, this must be balanced against the absolute generation of Rs 114 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 106 Cr in free cash flow during the exact same period [E28, E29, E30]. Conceded: borrowings expanded to Rs 991 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 910 Cr previously, but this debt load is offset by moderate overall leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.49x [E32, E34]. Regarding the bear's point on domestic institutional holdings decreasing to 12.68% and negative institutional money flow, promoter confidence has actually strengthened with promoter holding increasing to 64.04% alongside foreign institutional ownership rising to 3.27% [E36, E37, E38, E39]. Furthermore, the business commands superior operational efficiency compared to its peers, delivering a ROCE of 15.84% and an ROA of 6.1% versus sector benchmarks of 11.3% and 5.07% respectively [E8, E10].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 114 Cr and free cash flow reached Rs 106 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E30]. However, that absolute cash generation represents a severely depressed cash conversion of just 0.40x against reported profit, meaning operating cash flow was only 41% of operating profit and signaling that reported earnings significantly outpace actual cash realization [E28, E31]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a moderate 0.49x [E32]. Yet absolute borrowings expanded to Rs 991 Cr in March 2026 up from Rs 910 Cr a year earlier, adding financial weight as the current ratio tightens to a thin buffer of 1.60x [E33, E34]. Conceded: promoter holdings and foreign institutional ownership increased [E36, E37]. Despite those rises, domestic institutional holdings fell to 12.68% and overall institutional money flow registers as negative with a holding change of -2.28 percentage points, reflecting institutional distribution [E38, E39]. Finally, while superior ROCE and ROA metrics are cited [E8, E10], the company's historical ROE remains low at 13.2% over the last 3 years, and the yearly operating-margin trend is flagged as inconsistent [E26, E55].

Conceded: cash conversion sits at 0.40x with operating cash flow at 41% of operating profit, and borrowings expanded to Rs 991 Cr [E28, E31, E34]. However, the business still produced substantial absolute liquidity with Rs 114 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 106 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E29, E30], while maintaining a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.49x and an adequate current ratio of 1.60x [E32, E33]. Conceded: domestic institutions decreased holdings and overall institutional money flow is negative [E38, E39]. Yet, promoters strengthened their commitment by increasing their stake to 64.04% alongside a rise in foreign institutional ownership to 3.27% [E36, E37]. Finally, while the 3-year historical ROE is cited at 13.2% [E55], current annual metrics show a higher ROE of 14.7% and a strong ROCE of 17.0% [E12, E13], alongside superior profitability relative to sector benchmarks across ROA, ROCE, and EV/EBITDA [E8, E10, E11].

Conceded: the company produced Rs 114 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 106 Cr in free cash flow, and maintained a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.49x with a current ratio of 1.60x [E29, E30, E32, E33]. However, those absolute cash figures must be weighed against a poor cash conversion of 0.40x where operating cash flow is only 41% of operating profit, exposing severe profit-to-cash divergence and potential receivables or accrual strain [E28, E31]. Conceded: promoters increased their stake to 64.04% and foreign institutions added to 3.27% [E36, E37]. Yet, overall institutional money flow remains negative due to a withdrawal by domestic institutions lowering their stake to 12.68% [E38, E39]. Finally, while the bull highlights an ROE of 14.7% and ROCE of 17.0% [E12, E13], the company's multi-year performance suffers from a low 3-year historical ROE of 13.2% [E55] and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E26, E27].
